And when the Arabs of Acre sent to Saladin and informed him of the matter,
he gathered his nobles and took counsel with them.
And all of them said with one voice:
"These Arabs are our brothers,
and how can we abandon them?" And Saladin agreed to pay.
And immediately he sent to the provinces,
and gathered the Frankish prisoners.
And concerning the gold, he said
that every ten days he would pay a third.
And when ten days were completed, he sent to the Franks and said to them:
"Release therefore all the Arabs who are with you,
and we will give you a third of the gold and hostages for the other two thirds;
or else you give us hostages for the third of the gold that you receive."
And the Franks said:
"Our word alone is sufficient for you, and our good faith, which we give instead of hostages."
And the heart of Saladin hardened,
and he did not accept [this] from them.
Then the Franks became enraged, and bound all the Arabs with ropes,
and brought them out of the city onto a hill.
And they piled around them many logs of wood,
and old ropes,
and wine vessels which are called botte {OCR? vat / casks}:
like a wall.
And they drew swords and entered and slaughtered all of them,
while the advance guard of the Arabs stood and watched.
And the number of the Arabs who were killed on the walls of Acre,
and inside it,
and outside it on the hill,
mounted to one hundred thousand and eight hundred souls.
These things happened in the seventh month of the Arabs,
in the year 587,
[namely] 587 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1502,
[namely] 1502 of the Greeks,
(1191 of our Lord?) in the month of August.
And we have set forth a little regarding the memory of this expedition,
because it is very renowned among the Arabs,
and chronicles have recorded the tribulation that the Arabs endured at this time at the hands of the Franks.
And when the Franks took Acre,
they left in it a force sufficient for its defense,
and builders to repair its walls,
and they themselves set out towards Arsuf.
And Saladin likewise set out alongside them,
and they skirmished with one another every day as they traveled on the road.
